cards.d: A brook is a small stream.
cards.e: Water flows down several brooks on the mountain.

cards.d: To cater to someone means to provide them with all the things needed or wanted.
cards.e: Bill was too sick to get out of bed, so his nurse catered to his needs.

cards.d: When someone is considerate, they pay attention to the needs of others.
cards.e: The considerate boy gave a present to his girlfriend on Valentine’s Day.

cards.d: The consumption of food or drink is the act of eating or drinking it.
cards.e: These apples are too rotten for consumption.

cards.d: Criteria are factors on which a person judges or decides something.
cards.e: Before she got the job, she had to meet all the necessary criteria.

cards.d: Crust is the tough outer part of a loaf of bread.
cards.e: The little boy never ate the crust of his pizza.

cards.d: To degrade someone means to cause people to have shame.
cards.e: The teacher degraded Bob when she announced his poor performance to the class

cards.d: To entitle someone means to give them the rights to have or do something.
cards.e: His golden ticket entitled him to sit in the front row at the concert.

cards.d: To escort people means to safely accompany them to a place.
cards.e: Her bodyguards escorted her to the movie theater.

cards.d: When something is external, it is connected to an outer part.
cards.e: It is warm inside my house, but the external temperature is freezing.

cards.d: A facility is a building that exists for a particular purpose.
cards.e: There are many educational facilities in big cities.

cards.d: A faculty is a mental or physical ability.
cards.e: The boy’s mental faculties impressed all of his teachers.

cards.d: A heap of things is a large pile of them.
cards.e: After the building was torn down, all that was left was a heap of bricks.

cards.d: A hemisphere is one half of the earth.
cards.e: In the nor thern hemisphere, the weather is usually warmest in July and August.

cards.d: A hound is a type of dog that is often used for racing or hunting.
cards.e: The men took their hounds with them when they went on the hunting trip.

cards.d: If something is impersonal, it is not friendly and makes people feel unimportant.
cards.e: The boy felt scared on his first day at the big, impersonal high school.

cards.d: An ornament is an attractive object that people display in their homes.
cards.e: The woman kept some colorful ornaments on the shelves.

cards.d: A pedestrian is a person who is walking on a street.
cards.e: Cars should be careful when pedestrians are walking around.

cards.d: A sanctuary is a place where people in danger can go to be safe.
cards.e: The church was made into a sanctuary for homeless people in the winter.

cards.d: A spectator is someone who watches something, especially a sports event.
cards.e: There were thousands of spectators at the big game.
